text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today to close at $134.47, extending a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The drop follows the midterm election results, which handed a decisive victory to candidates favoring renewable energy expansion and a pullback from fossil fuel policies — a significant headwind for oil majors betting on sustained high energy demand. Crude oil prices have also softened, with US oil trading at $99.64 per barrel, down from the $146+ levels the stock was at just over a week ago.

The stock's weakness reflects a broader market rotation away from energy as the political landscape shifts. While geopolitical tensions with Iran persist and could theoretically support oil prices, the election outcome signaled investor concern that long-term energy policy will favor renewables, pressuring the outlook for traditional oil companies over the next several years.
